reviewer.persona: a recruiter and a hiring manager at an applied AI company

independence.note: Fictional example. Every person, organisation and quote here is made up.

six_second.read_as: An operations and quality program manager at a robotics company, not obviously an AI person.
six_second.why: The headline says what the person does, but nothing on the first screen shows AI work.
noticed_first: No link to any shipped work above the fold

roles.biggest_reason: Years running supplier and quality programs map straight onto fleet deployment.
Customer facing work is implied, never shown.
roles.biggest_gap: No customer or account work described

roles.biggest_reason: The posting asks for hands-on safety evaluation work; the profile shows none.
roles.biggest_gap: No evaluation or safety work a reviewer can check

red_flags.why: The CV says 30%. A reader who sees both trusts neither.
red_flags.fix: Use the number the person can prove, the same on every page.

red_flags.why: The CV gives the same role as Deputy Quality Manager. A background check will ask.
red_flags.fix: Use the title from the offer letter everywhere.

missing.why_it_matters: Proof a stranger can check is the strongest signal.

top_changes.change: Make the title and dates on LinkedIn match the CV and the offer letter.
top_changes.why: Removes the most obvious honesty question.

top_changes.change: Put one link to checkable work in the website headline area.
top_changes.why: The first screen shows no proof.

remove.quote: Ran the airline's external audit program
remove.why: Not on the CV or anywhere else; reads as an overclaim.

design_notes.note: On a phone the contact link is below three screens of text.

summary: Fictional example. Strong fit for operations heavy deployment roles; inconsistent titles and numbers between LinkedIn and the CV are the first thing to fix.
